name: Decline EZ-Bar Skull Crusher
description: The decline EZ-bar skull crusher uses a decline bench (typically -15 to -30 degrees) which moves the target area from the forehead downward, allowing the bar to travel further behind the head at the bottom of the movement. The decline angle places the medial and lateral heads under greater relative load compared to the flat version, and many lifters find the decline position more comfortable on the elbows. The extended range behind the head increases tricep stretch.

execution.starting_position: Set a bench to a slight decline. Secure feet. Lie back and have a spotter hand the EZ-bar to full extension above the lower chest/face.
execution.setup_instructions: Foot hooks are needed for the decline position. Keep the decline moderate (around 15 degrees).
steps: Step 1: Begin with EZ-bar above the chest/lower face at full elbow extension.
Step 2: Lower the bar by bending only the elbows, letting the bar travel toward and behind the head.
Step 3: Lower as far as comfortable without straining the elbows.
Step 4: Press back to the starting position by extending the elbows.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on descent, exhale on press.
common_mistakes: Letting the bar travel too far behind the head with heavy loads
Upper arms moving — keep them fixed
safety_considerations: The decline position makes the bar harder to control if dropped — always use a spotter
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension to bar behind the top of the head.
coaching_cues: Upper arms fixed — perpendicular to bench
Let the bar go behind the head
